quarterly_data.signal: AI AND CLOUD IS NOW NOKIA'S STRONGEST GROWTH DRIVER: AI-and-cloud net sales MORE THAN DOUBLED year-on-year to EUR 446 MILLION, with ORDER INTAKE OF EUR 2.8 BILLION in the quarter. Management context: Q2 benefited from several significant LONG-TERM ORDERS 'as our customers look to secure supply in A CONSTRAINED ENVIRONMENT'; roughly HALF of the Q2 order volume is expected to convert to revenue within 12 months, and order patterns are lumpy so this intake level should not be expected every quarter. Strength was broad-based across OPTICAL NETWORKS and IP NETWORKS, driven by growing demand for DATA CENTER INTERCONNECT and SCALE-ACROSS FABRICS, and included design wins flagged the prior quarter. Group Q2: net sales +9%, gross margin 46% (+70bps), operating margin 9% (+70bps); full-year operating profit tracking somewhat above the midpoint of guidance. Emerging second vector: telecom customers beginning to invest for AI-driven traffic growth.
quarterly_data.figure: AI & cloud sales 2x YoY to EUR 446M; order intake EUR 2.8B; ~half converts within 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: US INDIUM PHOSPHIDE AND OPTICAL CAPACITY BUILD-OUT ACROSS THREE SITES — explicitly framed against 'the supply constraints in the market today'. (1) SAN JOSE: the new indium phosphide fab is now PROCESSING TEST WAFERS as it moves toward product qualification, and remains ON TRACK FOR VOLUME PRODUCTION BY THE END OF 2026. (2) PENNSYLVANIA: a June commitment to scale the facility, increasing ADVANCED TEST AND PACKAGING capacity for optical systems there BY 10 TIMES. (3) ARIZONA: announced on this call, Nokia is ACQUIRING A MANUFACTURING SITE FROM NXP where it plans to increase indium phosphide fab capacity, giving 'additional capacity to support our own demand and greater optionality'. Together these are described as strengthening and securing US-based optical manufacturing capacity for the long term. Nokia is vertically integrating InP at the same time merchant suppliers report InP demand outpacing supply.
quarterly_data.figure: San Jose InP fab volume production by end-2026; Pennsylvania test/packaging 10x; NXP Arizona site acquired for InP

quarterly_data.signal: Product and design-win detail: secured its FIRST MULTI-RAIL ILA DESIGN WIN with a major customer — one of the new optical networking products launched at OFC in March 2026. Entered TRIALS WITH A US HYPERSCALER for a new OUT-OF-BAND MANAGEMENT solution that goes INSIDE the data center, leveraging the passive optical technology from Nokia's fixed networks business. Expanded partnership with GOOGLE CLOUD to bring Gemini-powered AI agents into Nokia's autonomous networks portfolio. Separately launched what it calls the industry's first commercial AI RAN platform (>100% spectral efficiency gains targeted by 2028; pilots at end of 2026, commercial availability 2027). Portfolio focus: fixed wireless access CPE and enterprise campus edge reclassified as DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS following a sale agreement with Inseego, on track to close by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: First multi-rail ILA design win; US hyperscaler trial for in-data-centre out-of-band management (passive optical)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 headline results (CEO/CFO): 'Net sales grew 4% to EUR 4.5 billion, with an operating margin of 6.2%, and we delivered a free cash flow of EUR 629 million.' Gross margin was 45.5%, up 320 basis points, 'supported in part by the absence of a one-time charge in Mobile Networks in the prior year' and also by 'strong performance in Optical Networks as we began to see the synergy benefits from the Infinera acquisition.' CFO: 'Optical Networks had another strong quarter with 20% net sales growth, and this was mainly driven by AI and cloud customers.' Network Infrastructure sales grew 6%; IP Networks grew 3%; Fixed Networks declined by 13%.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales EUR 4.5 billion (+4%); Optical Networks net sales growth 20%; gross margin 45.5%

quarterly_data.signal: AI and cloud momentum (CEO): 'We saw strong momentum with AI and cloud customers. Net sales grew 49% and we received EUR 1 billion in new orders, particularly driven by Optical Networks.' Book-to-bill was above one at group level and 'well above one' in Network Infrastructure. Orders show 'some elongation ... a desire for a longer-term commitment on orders'; only firm purchase orders with delivery dates are counted as orders, while multi-year frame agreements are not. Near-term demand is being fulfilled on 'our 800G pluggable and then the associated line systems and the platforms that we have available in shipping today.'
quarterly_data.figure: AI and cloud net sales +49%; EUR 1 billion in new AI and cloud orders

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance raised on optical/IP (CEO/CFO): Network Infrastructure growth now expected at 12%-14%, up from the 6%-8% communicated in January; Optical and IP Networks combined now 18%-20%, up from 10%-12%, with optimism 'across both sides of the business.' Drivers named by the CEO: 'a little bit more confidence on supply' (the fab plus DSPs and other optical subsystem components), strong optical demand, and IP networking traction. Growth is 'much more volume-driven than it is price-driven'; memory price increases are partly passed on to customers. Q2 assumes a 5%-9% sequential increase in net sales; group comparable operating profit outlook of EUR 2 billion-EUR 2.5 billion unchanged, tracking 'somewhat above the midpoint'.
quarterly_data.figure: Network Infrastructure 2026 growth 12%-14% (from 6%-8%); Optical and IP Networks 18%-20% (from 10%-12%); Q2 net sales +5%-9% sequential

quarterly_data.signal: Market sizing raised (CEO): since the November Capital Markets Day 'demand has accelerated' — expectations for the largest hyperscalers' 2026 CapEx rose from around $540 billion to over $700 billion. Nokia now expects its AI and cloud addressable market to grow at a 27% CAGR between 2025 and 2028, up from 16%, implying Network Infrastructure addressable market growth of 14% CAGR versus 9% before. Demand is seen in data center interconnect, inside the data center in routing and switching, and increasingly in metro and long-haul transport — 'a structural shift in the market which will sustain for multiple years.'
quarterly_data.figure: AI and cloud addressable market 27% CAGR 2025-2028 (from 16%); hyperscaler 2026 CapEx expectations over $700 billion (from around $540 billion)

quarterly_data.signal: OFC 2026 product launches (CEO): next-generation multi-rail in-line amplifier 'will begin shipping later this year' — 'an 8X increase in density, and is 25% more dense than competing products announced recently', addressing the scale from 'hundreds to thousands of fibers between data centers.' The optical roadmap moves to a building-block architecture with four optical engines embedded in multiple form factors (versus two engines per generation previously), enabling 13 application-optimized solutions and a TCO reduction of 'up to 70%'; 'These products will begin sampling in the first half of 2027 and will ship in volume in the second half.' The roadmap is 'largely oriented towards 2027' and was designed with AI and cloud customers. On co-packaged optics: 'At OFC, we demonstrated some technology development, but no announcements at this time.'
quarterly_data.figure: Multi-rail ILA 8X increase in density, begins shipping later this year; new optical engines begin sampling in first half of 2027, volume in second half; TCO reduction up to 70%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints and lead times (CEO/CFO): broader optical lead times are 'like, in the optical space is 12-18 months', with IP 'a little bit shorter'; the CEO pointed to ecosystem peers 'being sold out over multiple years' as 'a pretty good indication of where we see the Optical side.' 'There's a fair amount of constraint in the semiconductor ecosystem in general'; the industry's indium phosphide scale-up is 'driving demand back into the supply chain that we need to build capacity for.' CFO: 'supply is constrained. We are investing in securing that we get the supply that is needed' and 'Still there's more demand than supply.' Nokia is giving longer-term commitments back into its own supply chain.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical lead times 12-18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Indium phosphide capacity (CEO/CFO): the new indium phosphide manufacturing facility in San Jose, California (Fab 2) 'is on track to begin ramping production later this year.' 'Fab 2 is a fraction of the ramp for 2026. It's much more material to longer term'; guidance is 'risk balanced' for that ramp. Fab 2 gives 'the runway for the near term', and Nokia will 'look at ways to further accelerate capacity' as 'one of a few manufacturers with indium phosphide manufacturing capability at scale', though no additional capacity was announced. CFO: InP needs 'much lower CapEx' than silicon, and Fab 1 learnings are being transferred to Fab 2.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: Infinera integration and margins (CFO): Network Infrastructure gross margin was 43.4%, up 150 basis points, 'driven by a higher gross margin in Optical Networks, benefiting mainly from Infinera integration synergies and scale'; NI operating margin was 6.7%, 30 basis points lower on a full quarter of Infinera expenses. Synergy capture is 'on track or actually ahead of our targets', and the double-digit operating margin aim for optical set at the Infinera deal is still held. Some NI gross margin headwinds from product mix are expected through the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Network Infrastructure gross margin 43.4% (+150 basis points)

quarterly_data.signal: IP Networks / data-center switching (CEO/CFO): 'IP Networks sales grew 3%, with growth in AI and cloud offset by softness in other customer segments.' Nokia won new design wins with AI and cloud customers in Q1 that are 'in pipeline, but they're not in orders in Q1. We expect to see some of that start to flow in in Q2', and CFO expects IP Networks growth 'to start to accelerate in quarter two as we ramp shipments tied to new design wins.' The switching design-win footprint is 'certainly broader based on what we see today than it was a year ago.'
quarterly_data.figure: IP Networks sales +3%

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 headline results (CEO/CFO): 'Net sales grew 3% in the quarter to EUR 6.1 billion, with operating profit of EUR 1 billion and free cash flow of EUR 0.2 billion. For the full year, net sales were EUR 19.9 billion and operating profit was EUR 2 billion, slightly above the midpoint of our guidance.' Network Infrastructure: 'In the fourth quarter, net sales grew 7%, driven by optical networks, which grew by 17%.' Group gross margin was 48.1%, 'an improvement of 90 basis points'. Network Infrastructure gross margin 'declined by 80 basis points to 44.6%', and its operating margin 'was impacted by lower gross margin, along with the increased growth-related investments in R&D and the costs associated with the acquisition of Infinera.'
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales grew 3% to EUR 6.1 billion; Network Infrastructure grew 7%; optical networks grew by 17%; FY2025 net sales EUR 19.9 billion; Network Infrastructure gross margin 44.6%

quarterly_data.signal: AI and cloud orders and mix (CEO/CFO): 'For the full year 2025, we delivered EUR 2.4 billion in orders from AI and cloud customers.' Q4 Network Infrastructure 'Order intake was solid across both optical and IP networks with a book-to-bill above 1, supported by particularly strong demand from AI and cloud customers.' CFO, in the Network Infrastructure discussion: 'In quarter 4, AI & Cloud customers accounted for 16% of our net sales and 30% of Optical Networks.' On Optical and IP book-to-bill separately: 'Each one is healthy on the book-to-bill.' The CEO framed the optical base as 'still very telco-centric in '25, so 70-30', with Nokia 'really only three quarters deep in terms of aggressively pursuing the AI & Cloud segment'; the CFO added that 'where we see growth is AI & Cloud in North America'.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 2.4 billion AI and cloud orders in FY2025; AI & Cloud customers accounted for 16% of our net sales and 30% of Optical Networks in Q4 (CFO, Network Infrastructure discussion)

quarterly_data.signal: 800G coherent pluggable ramp (CEO): 'In Optical, our 800-gig ZR and ZR+ pluggable products are shipping with initial units performing well in the field. We now have multiple design wins and are supplying into scale deployments. Our focus is on ramping production to meet the strong demand we see in the market.' In Q&A: 'We're ramping on 800-gig multiple pluggable wins, as we've talked about, a lot of active customer conversations on that space'.
quarterly_data.figure: 800-gig ZR and ZR+ pluggables shipping; multiple design wins; supplying into scale deployments

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-across and speed transitions (CEO): scale-across data center interconnect is 'one of the most significant near term' drivers of optical demand. 'We've gone through the 400- and 800-gig transition very quickly.' 'we expect that 1.6 and 3.2 will come. And when you look at that scale across is the tailwind for both the technology transitions and the demand. And then, of course, over time, we see scale out increasingly be an opportunity for coherent optics.' Scale-across is also a tailwind for routing ('switching is much more about the data center racks, the spine-leaf architecture'). Later: 'Scale across is an emerging opportunity' and 'over time, as speeds continue to ramp within the data center, there will be more opportunity for coherent optics within the data center.' He described 'a much more mature and larger optical market, driven by the AI infrastructure build-out than we've seen in the past.'
quarterly_data.figure: 400- and 800-gig transition passed very quickly; 1.6 and 3.2 will come; coherent optics moving toward scale out / inside the data center over time

quarterly_data.signal: IP Networks data center switching (CEO): 'we made progress on our expansion into data center switching. We launched two new products in the quarter, the 7220 IXR-H6 switching platform powered by Broadcom's TH6 and our Agentic AI solution for event-driven automation management'. 'We also secured a design win for our next-generation data center switching platform.' In Q&A the CEO said this is 'a space where I think it's going to take us a little bit of time to see the growth', that he is 'pleased with the order backlog', but 'this business needs a little bit of time to ramp'; a new Head of IP Networking was brought in with 'deep data center experience'.
quarterly_data.figure: 7220 IXR-H6 switching platform (Broadcom's TH6) launched; design win for next-generation data center switching platform

quarterly_data.signal: Original 2026 outlook and 2028 KPIs (CEO/CFO, January): 'in 2026, we are targeting an operating profit in the range of EUR 2 billion to EUR 2.5 billion.' KPI: '6% to 8% compound annual growth in network infrastructure between 2025 and 2028' and '10% to 12% in the combined Optical and IP Networks businesses. In 2026, we expect growth rates in both cases to be in line with these long-term targets.' Network Infrastructure operating margin target '13% to 17% by 2028', 'compared to the 9.5% achieved in 2025', with 'measured margin expansion as we ramp new products' in 2026. The CEO said Nokia is 'being balanced on the 10% to 12% across IP and Optical Networking', citing a base that was 'still very telco-centric in '25' and that 'in parallel, we're working to scale production'. The CFO expects Q1 2026 net sales 'to decline somewhat more than normal seasonality would imply' and second-half Network Infrastructure margins better than first-half as new products launched in the first half ramp.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 operating profit EUR 2 billion to EUR 2.5 billion; Network Infrastructure growth 6% to 8% and Optical and IP Networks 10% to 12% in 2026; Network Infrastructure operating margin 13% to 17% by 2028 (9.5% in 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Optical manufacturing CapEx and indium phosphide fab (CFO/CEO): 'we are planning for CapEx of between EUR 900 million and EUR 1 billion as we invest in additional manufacturing capacity for Optical Networks, along with some real estate renewal projects.' CEO: 'we have an existing fab in California. We've been investing in bringing a new fab online. This is something that Infinera had started before we acquired them', with 'partial funding in the CHIPS Act from the U.S. government'; the new indium phosphide fab is 'the one we expect to come online later this year.' 'we're certainly well on track to consume capacity in the existing one, and we absolutely need the new fab to come online to support the demand that we're seeing and to meet our forecast.' 'I would think about the investments we're making really in that new fab supporting '27 demand. They're starting to ramp during '27.' 'at the core of our capability and our differentiation is our photonic integrated circuit'; Nokia sees 'tremendous value in that vertical integration'.
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx EUR 900 million to EUR 1 billion (2026) for additional Optical Networks manufacturing capacity along with some real estate renewal projects; new indium phosphide fab online later this year, supporting '27 demand

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints and memory (CEO): 'we do see supply constraints that's normal with this kind of scale and build. And obviously, part of our investments is not just in our own capacity but also in supporting the ecosystem and building its capability and capacity.' Optical 'is not nearly running at the kinds of volumes' of the microelectronics industry, which is 'part of why we think we're favorably positioned with our indium phosphide technology and manufacturing facility.' On rising memory prices: memory is 'not a huge part of our bill of materials'; Nokia is focused on securing 'the supply based on the commitments we have' under long-term agreements and expects the cost 'to be passed through to pricing'; 'the supply agreements are multiyear and then pricing varies depending on the contract term.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure

quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA partnership and equity investment (CEO/CFO): 'in Q4, we announced our partnership with NVIDIA. quarterly_data.signal: CPO TEST - TIMING AND WHERE VIAVI SITS: Khaykin said Viavi has been working on a CPO test 'now for well over 12 to close to 2 years. We are now started shipping, I would say even this quarter is early shipments.' Test capacity is facilitized ahead of demand and the next increment is added at about '60%, 70% utilization'. CPO pulls Viavi into semiconductor test next to Advantest, Teradyne and FormFactor - the configuration is an IC tester plus a prober plus an optical rack, all interconnected - and he expects a HIGHER share for Viavi there than in pluggables because Viavi sells an automatable integrated platform with '2,500 SKUs' of measurement modules rather than a point solution. Content per port rises sharply: pluggable is power, dispersion and insertion loss, CPO is multiple insertions plus extensive functional test, with known-good-die, optical-engine and interconnect-platform insertions all before the ASIC and memory go on a module worth 'thousands of dollars' - skip them and 'you will be throwing away tens of millions of dollars'.

quarterly_data.signal: AI test intensity is compounding because design margins are shrinking: higher data rates, lower latency and the requirement that AI fabrics be LOSSLESS mean customers 'can no longer guarantee anything by design' and must test in production too. A compute or switch tray has gone from tens to HUNDREDS of IC pinouts - more insertion points - tested at signal level (VNAs, oscilloscopes), at bit level (new portfolio) and at protocol/packet level (AI workload emulators). The move from monolithic chips to CHIPLET architectures adds interoperability emulation, and customers now ask for emulation environments that stress a chip while it exercises a model (thermal shutdown, all cores active at higher power and speed). The ecosystem is shifting from a homogeneous integrated vertical stack to a HETEROGENEOUS one - GPU/CPU/DPU mixes and a growing number of protocols at every layer of the stack - which broadens Keysight's addressable tail. The four wireline pillars (AI infrastructure scaling, speed transitions, silicon photonics, system-level emulation) all drove growth. Hyperscaler engagement (rooted in the Ixia acquisition ~5 years ago) is deepening as they integrate Keysight pre-silicon emulation and workload solutions into their development pipelines; hyperscalers plus the model companies are ~10% OF REVENUE DIRECTLY but drive large downstream influence, and many are building their own in-house silicon. Switch designers use Keysight emulators to validate network performance across AI workloads and protocols; interconnect manufacturers use high-fidelity analyzers to characterize high-speed backplanes for signal integrity and manufacturing yield.
quarterly_data.figure: Hundreds of IC pinouts per tray; hyperscalers ~10% of revenue direct; chiplet + workload emulation

CSG President Kailash Narayanan: 'quite a bit of activity at this moment going on from the perspective of 1.6 terabit R&D as well as 448 gig per lane and 3.2 tera R&D'; scale-up and scale-out are both opportunities in R&D and manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: data center build-outs with 800 gig and 1.6 tera optics; accelerated development of 3.2 tera; 448 gig per lane

quarterly_data.signal: Optical interconnects (CEO): 'Rising bandwidth and power demands in AI data centers are accelerating the adoption of optical interconnects to supplement copper.' Keysight is helping optical transceiver and module suppliers ramp and design their 800-gig and emerging 1.6-terabit modules with its recently introduced Digital Communication Analyzer and Lightwave Component Analyzer products. 'Concurrently, customers are designing architectures around co-packaged optics, optical circuit switching and silicon photonics'; Keysight's tunable laser sources and polarization synthesizers provide metrology-grade measurements for silicon photonics workflows, and its workload emulation solutions help leading customers emulate real AI workload and stress conditions as clusters scale.
quarterly_data.figure: 800-gig and emerging 1.6-terabit modules

contracts.signal: AXT 'recently signed strategic LONG-TERM SUPPLY AGREEMENTS' with Coherent (announced alongside a second partner and, the same week, Lumentum). CEO Morris Young: these agreements 'deepen our relationship with these important customers, working shoulder to shoulder with them to help them deliver on their own vision and road maps' and gave AXT 'even greater sense of conviction that our capacity build out is mirrored and necessary.'

AXT-Tongmei entered a Master Development and Supply Agreement with Coherent Corp (signed June 26, 2026, effective June 25, 2026) for the mass development and supply of 6-inch indium phosphide wafer substrates for an initial term of three years. AXT agreed to increase manufacturing capacity for these products at its Beijing facility in 2026 through 2028 and committed an agreed product capacity to Coherent in exchange for a prepayment of US$22,288,500 from Coherent, applied to product purchases at agreed per-wafer prices; additional capacity beyond the committed quantity is to be offered to Coherent on the same terms.

contracts.signal: AXT announced a strategic long-term supply agreement with LUMENTUM in the week of the Q2 call, following similar agreements with Coherent and one other partner. AXT frames these LTAs as confirmation that its InP capacity build-out is 'mirrored and necessary' against customer road maps.

Lumentum confirmed the AXT indium phosphide substrate deal from the buyer side, signed during its fiscal Q4 (quarter ended 06-27-2026). Trigger was a surge in ultra-high-power (CPO/NPO) laser demand across a couple of customers that outran Lumentum's existing substrate arrangements: 'we have seen a pretty big surge in demand... in order to respond to that, we went out and we found additional substrate help from AXT.' Lumentum expects it may need still more substrate supply if the demand vector continues.

On July 26, 2026 AXT and Lumentum Operations LLC entered a Capacity Reservation Agreement for the supply and capacity reservation of indium phosphide wafer substrates: AXT reserves a minimum annual commitment of the products for Lumentum for a six-year period (the press release says through December 31, 2031) and will support additional capacity if required. Lumentum pays an initial deposit of $43,500,000 within thirty business days and a second deposit of $43,500,000 with timing and terms to be determined during calendar year 2028; the deposits are applied as shipment credits, and Lumentum is responsible for any shortfall below its annual purchase commitment.

INDIUM PHOSPHIDE revenue $30.7M, also an all-time company record, 'primarily from data center applications' (vs $13.6M in Q1 — more than doubled sequentially); gallium arsenide $6.6M; germanium $0.27M; consolidated raw-material JVs $10M. Non-GAAP gross margin 45.0% versus 29.9% in Q1 and just 8.2% a year ago; non-GAAP operating profit $11.2M versus a $6.1M loss a year ago; non-GAAP opex $10.2M; inventory $96.3M. Customer concentration low: top five customers ~30% of revenue with NO customer above 10%. InP revenue in China's laser market MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially (no export permit required for shipments within China). Q3 2026 guidance: ~$66M of revenue already realizable across substrates and raw materials where permits are in hand or not required — with possible 'significant upside' if additional export permits arrive (timing unpredictable); non-GAAP EPS $0.30-0.32 on ~66.5M shares.

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY AND DEMAND: AXT is AHEAD OF SCHEDULE on its commitment to DOUBLE InP capacity in 2026, and now reports the InP revenue opportunity is 'on track to MORE THAN TRIPLE by the end of 2026' with significant further expansion expected in 2027; it is well into planning to DOUBLE CAPACITY AGAIN IN 2027 at an adjacent location, which management says 'will make AXT by far the largest indium phosphide producer in the world'. Backlog 'continues to grow and is now WELL OVER $100 MILLION'; 'customer demand continues to outpace supply no matter how fast we add capacity.' Three drivers of the step-function: faster-than-expected capacity expansion, productivity gains from NEW CRYSTAL GROWTH FURNACE DESIGNS, and customers moving to LARGER-DIAMETER substrates and higher-value products with favorable pricing. Progress reported on 6-INCH InP capability ('exponentially more difficult to produce in volume than 3- or 4-inch'). Supply structure: high-quality InP is limited to just a few players on technical barriers; AXT's vertically integrated JVs now include subsidiary Jingmei refining HIGH-PURITY INDIUM in-house.
quarterly_data.figure: InP revenue to MORE THAN TRIPLE by end-2026; capacity 2x in 2026 and 2x again 2027; backlog >$100M

quarterly_data.signal: DEMAND DRIVERS AND CUSTOMERS: optical connectivity deployment in AI data centers is accelerating 'as hyperscalers scale GPU dense architectures and look for higher speed lower power photonics'. Near term the pull is the industry migration to 1.6T transceiver modules, 'for which indium phosphide based lasers and detectors are essential'; longer term, hyperscalers advancing toward NEAR-PACKAGED AND CO-PACKAGED OPTICS 'will continue to drive increasing demand for our material' — pointing to a durable multiyear demand cycle. AXT signed strategic LONG-TERM SUPPLY AGREEMENTS with COHERENT and another partner, and announced one with LUMENTUM the week of the call. US cloud/AI capex is the primary driver for EML and silicon-photonics transceivers plus high-speed photodetectors; AXT believes its material is used at MULTIPLE US HYPERSCALERS with end-customer use expected to broaden, alongside 'huge growth in China'. Corporate: subsidiary Tongmei withdrew its STAR Market IPO application (06-26-2026) and is redirecting to a HONG KONG EXCHANGE listing (~1 year); this created a redemption right on $49M of 2021 PE investment, though those investors currently wish to remain.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T migration + CPO/NPO drive multiyear InP cycle; LTAs with Coherent and Lumentum; Tongmei to HKEX

CEO Morris Young: 'We were disappointed that we didn't receive as many export permits in Q4 as we had hoped'; permits have since been received in Q1 and AXT expects sequential revenue growth in Q1 'driven primarily by growth in indium phosphide for data center build-out for AI'. CFO: approximately $26 million of Q1 revenue across substrate product lines and raw materials can be realized because AXT already holds a permit or none is required, with 'significant upside' possible if more permits arrive before quarter-end (no usual range given). quarterly_data.signal: Export-permit process (VP Business Development Tim Bettles): the China permit process 'is not transparent at all'; the fairly consistent 60 business day cycle seen at the end of Q3 has given way to 'a lot more variability', and 'It's reasonable to assume that there's geopolitics playing into this'. AXT received its first-ever permit denials, which came with instructions to resubmit with more information; they have been resubmitted to MOFCOM (China's Ministry of Commerce), and a quick turnaround could affect Q1. Once a permit is received AXT has a 6-month window to export, so backlog builds around permit timing. CEO: receipt of indium phosphide and gallium arsenide export licenses 'remains the single most significant gating factor for our growth'.
quarterly_data.figure: first permit denials received (resubmitted to MOFCOM); 60 business day cycle now highly variable; 6-month export window per permit

quarterly_data.signal: InP demand and backlog: CEO says the backlog for indium phosphide wafers 'have reached a new high of over $60 million', with customers placing longer-term orders and giving more visibility; 'we definitely have more orders than we can actually manufacture now'. Customers told AXT in meetings that week that 'our demand forecast increases every week'. Tim Bettles: AXT is 'talking about long-term supply agreements with a number of customers right now' (customers not named) and sees forecasts out beyond 2030, with customers discussing minimum demand requirements for at least the next 2 to 3 years; customers are also committing through NRE and purchase orders. CFO: AXT is meeting CEOs and general managers rather than purchasing managers, who say 'their demand is going to be going up 3, 4 or 5x over the next 4 or 5 years'.
quarterly_data.figure: InP backlog new high of over $60 million; customer forecasts out beyond 2030

quarterly_data.signal: InP capacity plan and cost: since October AXT has added approximately 25% more capacity and is on track to double capacity from the Q4 2025 level by the end of 2026. CEO: this first phase costs 'about $30 million', which is on the low end because it is mainly brownfield inside the existing Tongmei facility (clean room, building, power and water already in place). Beyond 2026 AXT is 'looking at possibly doubling it again in 2027' with a budget of $100 million to $150 million because that phase is greenfield. The CEO puts year-end InP capacity at 'approximately $35 million a quarter' run rate (possibly more as indium costs rise) and says the backlog can absorb it, with permits as the gating factor. The recent capital raise 'will be fundamental to our future expansion'.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 25% more capacity added since October; about $30 million to double capacity by end of 2026; $100 million to $150 million to possibly double again in 2027; approximately $35 million a quarter InP capacity run rate by the end of the year

quarterly_data.signal: Customer base and China: CEO says the InP customer base is expanding to 'Tier 1 laser manufacturers and optical transceiver module makers both in China and around the world' where AXT previously had limited exposure, helped by its low EPD wafers as optics move to higher speed for scale-up and scale-out (customers not named). Tim Bettles: AXT is winning design-ins and qualifications on existing and new products. China's data center build-out is 'early in its ramp', and AXT's China data center revenue is expected to grow by more than 60% in Q1 over Q4, which the CEO says highlights increased investment in Tier 1 data centers and 'the strong desire for Chinese domestic suppliers to secure local' supply 'at every level of the AI infrastructure supply chain'. Bettles adds that Q4 China revenue was probably double Q1 2025, with potential to double again through 2026. CFO: the Tongmei STAR Market IPO application remains current and 'in process', with China's AI infrastructure build-out 'fueling increased China-based demand for indium phosphide substrates'.
quarterly_data.figure: China data center revenue expected to grow by more than 60% in Q1 over Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Wafer-size transition: Tim Bettles says 'there's already been a big move from 3-inch to 4-inch' and AXT has scaled up its 4-inch business; 'we all know one customer that's really driving 6-inch demand' (customer not named), so AXT is 'looking at adding significant 6-inch capacity' as it doubles capacity through 2026 and beyond. CEO: a major focus of the expansion is more investment in 6-inch InP for 'next-generation EML and silicon photonic-based devices', and customers are deciding how much to switch 'from 3 to 4 and 4 to 6'. Larger sizes normally bring better margins, but 6-inch is 'still a little bit in development stage', with lower margins at first; the product mix is still 'very much geared towards 3-inch and 4-inch'.
quarterly_data.figure: big move from 3-inch to 4-inch already made; significant 6-inch capacity to be added as capacity doubles through 2026 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: Co-packaged optics timing: beyond pluggable transceivers, the CEO sees 'a very large developing market for co-packaged optics for both scale-up and scale-out applications'. AXT is discussing technical and timing requirements with customers and believes CPO could be another inflection point for its business 'developing in late 2027 and beyond'.
quarterly_data.figure: co-packaged optics inflection developing in late 2027 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: Margin framework: the CFO says that at 'somewhere at $40 million a quarter in aggregate, not just indium phosphide', AXT should be 'hopefully somewhere close to 35% gross margin', and the internal goal is higher. The CEO says 35% reflects the normal substrate business, and growth there should also lift the vertically integrated raw-material businesses (indium, phosphorus, quartz, PBN crucibles, furnaces) and add margin. Supply-chain control: 'JinMei makes the indium phosphide poly for Tongmei', a subsidiary makes the PBN crucibles used in InP manufacturing, and the raw material business grew in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: hopefully close to 35% gross margin at $40 million a quarter in aggregate revenue
